scenes.narration: Optel shows who those visitors are. {col1}Where they come from: search, ads, AI assistants, our own portal. {col2}Which device. {col3}Then the first rule that matches. {col4}And the homepage experience that rule picks.
{p1}<largest cohort>: <share in words>. {p2}<most valuable cohort>: <share>. {p3}<third cohort>: <share>, and this one is modelled from what visitors did, until the site remembers them.
Customers coming back from the portal {new}now get sign-in and their top tasks first. {ring}The rest of the page is still there, below.
{orig}On a phone, the first visit looked like this. {new}Now it starts with the tasks phones come for. {fewer}And it is a much shorter page.

{f1}The choice is made in the browser, before the page paints. {f2}No personal data: referrer, campaign tags, device, and a visit memory on the device only. {f3}Every rule is a few lines that authors can read.
Ten percent keep today's homepage. That holdout tells us, rule by rule, every month, whether the new first view does better. And one setting switches it all off.

scenes.title: One homepage. A first view that fits.
